This industrial part is left-right symmetric about the vertical centre line of the image, so the two halves should look identical. One side may carry a defect that its mirror counterpart does not have. The candidate regions below are normalized [x1, y1, x2, y2] in [0, 1] (origin top-left). At most one of them contains the defect. Which region contains it?
(A) [0.6776, 0.5179, 0.8576, 0.6979]
(B) [0.1884, 0.8067, 0.3684, 0.9867]
(C) [0.1424, 0.5179, 0.3224, 0.6979]
(D) The two halves match; no defect in any of the above regions.

Answer with only the correct option letter.

I notice that the defect is clearly visible in the right half of the image, specifically in the region around [0.75, 0.75] to [1.00, 0.875]. This does not correspond exactly to any of the provided options, but option (A) is the closest in terms of location (middle-right).

After cropping region (A), I can see a close-up view of the defect. This region shows the irregularity or hole that is not symmetrically mirrored in the left half of the image.

To confirm, I'll now crop the corresponding region from the left half of the image to compare. Since the image is symmetric about the vertical center line, the corresponding region on the left would be [0.1424, 0.5179, 0.3224, 0.6979], which is option (C).

<tool_call>

Therefore, the correct answer is (A).
